story.title: Self-service password reset
story.description: Let customers reset a forgotten password themselves from web-banking and mobile-banking. The authentication-service issues a single-use reset token that expires in 15 minutes and enforces the password policy; the notification-service sends the reset link by email and SMS; customer-db records the last reset time and failed reset attempts. Reset requests must not reveal whether an account exists.
acceptance_criteria: A customer can request a reset link and set a new password that meets the password policy.
Reset tokens are single use and expire after 15 minutes.
The response is identical whether or not the account exists.
Five reset requests in an hour block further requests for that customer.

requirement.business_summary: Customers will be able to reset a forgotten password themselves from web-banking and mobile-banking instead of relying on assisted servicing. Authentication Service issues a single-use reset token valid for 15 minutes and enforces the password policy; Notification Service delivers the reset link by email and SMS; Customer Database records the last reset time and failed reset attempts. Reset requests return an identical response whether or not the account exists, and five requests in an hour block further requests for that customer.
requirement.technical_summary: Add a self-service password reset flow: Authentication Service gains reset-token issuance/validation (single use, 15-minute expiry), password-policy enforcement, uniform request responses to prevent account enumeration, and per-customer rate limiting of five reset requests per hour. Web and mobile channels add request-reset and set-new-password UI and call the new endpoints. Notification Service sends the reset link over email and SMS. Customer Database stores the last reset time and failed reset attempt count for the customer. No card or financial/ledger data is involved.
requirement.business_domain: Identity and Access Management / Retail Banking Self-Service
affected_capabilities: Reset token issuance and expiry control
Reset request rate limiting / abuse prevention
Email and SMS notification delivery for security events
requirement.engineering_scope: Contained, single-flow change. Authentication Service: new reset-token issue/validate logic (single use, 15-minute expiry), password-policy enforcement on the new password, identical responses regardless of account existence, and a per-customer limit of five reset requests per hour. Web Banking and Mobile Banking: add request-reset and set-new-password screens wired to those endpoints. Notification Service: send the reset link via existing email and SMS channels. Customer Database: persist last reset time and failed reset attempt count for the customer record. No changes to payment, card, loan or ledger processing; no changes to existing public contracts beyond adding the new self-service endpoints.

dimensions.name: operational

dimensions.name: performance
dimensions.explanation: Performance risk is medium (40) because transaction path (+20) on payment-service, transaction-db; channel path (+15) on api-gateway, mobile-banking, web-banking.

dimensions.name: delivery

tests.title: Security risk dimension: Password reset request returns identical response for existing and non-existing accounts
steps: From Web Banking, submit a password reset request for a known existing customer account.
Capture the HTTP status, response body and user-visible message.
From Mobile Banking, submit a password reset request for an account identifier that does not exist.
Capture the HTTP status, response body and user-visible message.
Compare both responses for content and shape.
tests.expected: Both requests return an identical response regardless of account existence; no message or status reveals whether the account exists.

tests.title: Security risk dimension: Reset token is single-use and expires after 15 minutes
steps: Request a password reset for an existing customer from Web Banking.
Obtain the reset link delivered by Notification Service.
Use the reset token once to set a new password that satisfies the password policy.
Attempt to reuse the same reset token to set another password.
Request a new reset token, wait 16 minutes, then attempt to use it.
tests.expected: The first token sets the password once; reuse is rejected as invalid; the second token is rejected after its 15-minute expiry; the Customer Database records reset activity.

tests.title: Compliance risk dimension: Password reset events are recorded in Audit Database without secrets
steps: Perform a successful self-service password reset from Web Banking.
Query Audit Database for the reset event using the customer identifier and correlation identifier.
Inspect the stored event fields for customer identifier, event type, outcome, timestamp and correlation identifier.
Verify no password, reset token or token secret is present in the audit event.
tests.expected: Audit Database contains an immutable reset event with the required compliance fields; no credential or token secret is stored.

tests.title: Technical risk dimension: Customer Database persists last reset time and failed reset attempt count
steps: Trigger three failed set-new-password attempts for a customer using passwords that violate the password policy.
Perform one successful password reset for the same customer.
Read the customer record through the internal customer-store profile endpoint.
tests.expected: Customer Database stores the last reset time and failed reset attempt count; the failed count reflects the three rejected attempts before the successful reset.

tests.title: Operational risk dimension: Sixth password reset request in one hour is blocked for the same customer
steps: From Web Banking, submit five password reset requests for the same customer within one hour.
Submit a sixth password reset request for the same customer.
Check whether Notification Service sends another reset link.
tests.expected: The first five requests are accepted with uniform responses; the sixth request is blocked by per-customer rate limiting and no additional reset link is delivered.

tests.title: Password reset notification uses verified email and SMS preferences from Customer Service and CRM
steps: Ensure the customer has a verified email address and verified mobile number in Customer Service and CRM.
Request a password reset from Mobile Banking.
Verify Notification Service sends the reset link by both email and SMS.
Mark the email address as unverified in CRM and request another password reset.
tests.expected: The first reset delivers to both verified email and SMS; the second reset does not deliver to the unverified email and still uses the verified SMS destination.

tests.title: Password reset does not create card, payment, or ledger activity
steps: Capture baseline card status, payment instruction count and transaction ledger entries for a customer.
Perform a successful self-service password reset from Web Banking.
Re-query card status, payment records and transaction ledger entries for the same customer.
tests.expected: Card status, payment records and transaction ledger remain unchanged; the password reset flow creates no card, payment or ledger posting.

tests.title: Password reset rollout leaves assisted, lending, reporting, document, and risk nodes unchanged
steps: Capture baseline behavior for ATM withdrawal, Branch Portal service request, Loan Service application, Reporting Service monthly statement job, Risk Engine assessment and Document Service template rendering.
Perform a successful self-service password reset from Web Banking.
Re-run the ATM, Branch Portal, Loan Service, Reporting Service, Risk Engine and Document Service checks.
tests.expected: Assisted, lending, reporting, risk and document behaviors remain unchanged; the password reset rollout does not alter their existing public contracts or processing.

tests.summary: Selected 15 catalog tests and 8 new tests, covering 20 of 20 impacted nodes (100%); estimated effort is 13.2 hours.

frameworks.reason: PII-bearing components are impacted; the change touches customer data.

findings.text: The change adds processing of personal data such as password reset tokens, reset timestamps, and failed attempt counts in authentication-service, web-banking, mobile-banking, notification-service, and customer-db, which are PII-bearing components.
Schema updates to customer-db to persist last reset time and failed reset attempt count affect data retention and purpose limitation obligations under GDPR.
Authentication flow modifications may impact data minimization and consent requirements, necessitating verification that only necessary personal data is collected for the reset flow.

recommendations: Review data minimization, purpose, and retention for the password reset personal data in authentication-service, web-banking, mobile-banking, notification-service, and customer-db to ensure compliance with GDPR principles.

Verify that access controls and privacy regression tests are updated for authentication-service, web-banking, mobile-banking, notification-service, and customer-db to protect the new personal data fields.
Ensure that the reset token expiry and single-use enforcement are documented and tested to limit unnecessary retention of personal data.
Confirm that customer-db updates include appropriate data retention schedules and that deletion or anonymization mechanisms are in place for reset-related fields.

findings.text: The change modifies authentication-service, which is involved in authentication for card-related transactions, though no cardholder data is directly stored or transmitted in the password reset flow.

Components that handle card data (atm, card-service, fraud-engine, mobile-banking, web-banking, notification-service) remain in scope; any changes to authentication could affect card data security controls.
Database schema changes to customer-db do not involve card data, but ensure that any linkage between customer records and card data is not inadvertently altered.

recommendations: Verify that authentication-service changes do not weaken card data protection controls, including token handling and session management for atm, card-service, fraud-engine, mobile-banking, web-banking, and notification-service.

Review encryption, masking, and access restrictions for card data in atm, card-service, fraud-engine, mobile-banking, web-banking, and notification-service to ensure they remain effective after the authentication flow updates.
Run card-data security tests focused on authentication and API controls for atm, authentication-service, card-service, fraud-engine, mobile-banking, notification-service, and web-banking.
Confirm that any updates to customer-db preserve the separation between personal data and cardholder data fields.

frameworks.reason: financial-data components are impacted; audit-data components are impacted.

findings.text: The change modifies authentication-service, web-banking, mobile-banking, notification-service, and customer-db, which support access to financial applications but do not directly process financial data.

Financial data processing components such as account-service, payment-service, transaction-db, loan-service, and risk-engine rely on authentication; changes to authentication could affect financial reporting controls.
Audit database (audit-db) captures authentication events; ensure that audit logging remains complete and immutable for SOX compliance.

recommendations: Reconcile that financial reporting controls remain effective by verifying that authentication changes do not alter access to financial systems like account-service, payment-service, transaction-db, loan-service, and risk-engine.
Document control-owner approval and test financial and schema changes for audit-db to ensure immutable audit records of authentication events.
Verify that audit-db continues to capture complete, immutable audit events for authentication-related activities supporting SOX requirements.
Ensure that any changes to customer-db do not affect financial data integrity or the ability to trace financial transactions.

frameworks.reason: directly changed components have criticality >= 8; the authentication flow changes.

findings.text: Directly changed components include high-criticality services authentication-service (criticality 10), customer-db (9), mobile-banking (8), web-banking (8), and notification-service (6), triggering internal governance review.
The authentication flow changes introduce new reset-token issuance, validation, and rate‑limiting logic, which may affect operational stability and require governance oversight.
Database schema updates to customer-db to store reset timestamps and failed attempt counts alter critical data and need change‑management controls.

recommendations: Obtain service‑owner change approval and record a detailed rollback plan for authentication-service, customer-db, mobile-banking, web-banking, and notification-service.
Verify authorization tests, operational monitoring, and release evidence for authentication-service, customer-db, mobile-banking, web-banking, and notification-service.
Confirm that the new reset-token logic includes appropriate unit and integration tests, and that monitoring alerts are in place for anomalous reset‑request patterns.
Ensure that the customer-db schema changes are reviewed by data‑ownership and that backup and recovery procedures cover the new fields.

rollback_plan: Roll back in reverse deployment order, starting with channels-mobile (mobile-banking) then channels-access (atm, branch-portal, web-banking), and disable any configured reset-flow feature flags.

Continue with identity (api-gateway, authentication-service), documents (document-service) and data-platform (audit-db, reporting-service), pausing on any monitoring anomaly and notifying the release owner and stakeholders.

Finish with customer-platform (crm, customer-db, customer-service, notification-service), core-payments and core-banking, restoring the database groups from verified backups, running the rehearsed DB migration rollback and reconciling reset-activity data.
deployment_notes: Hold production deployment for this NO_GO decision; these notes are preparation for a later approved release only and no rollout may begin without a new go decision.

Before any approved rollout, verify backups, rehearse the Customer Database migration rollback and data reconciliation, and apply backward-compatible migrations ahead of services in the fixed order core-banking, core-payments, customer-platform, data-platform, documents, identity, channels-access, channels-mobile.

On an approved release, enable the reset-flow feature flags where configured, monitor token issuance, rate-limit blocks, notification delivery and failed reset attempts, and have the release owner send stakeholder updates at each gate.
